WARNING: TEST-ONLY KEY MATERIAL. The all-zero entropy below is the standard public BIP-39 vector and has no secrecy whatsoever. It exists to prove the reconstruction path. NEVER use it as a production identity, and never treat a real recovery phrase this way: a real phrase is private-key-equivalent and must not enter this repository, a log, a diagnostic, or any file (CLAUDE.md §6, ADR-0033).

steps: entropy is exactly 32 bytes and IS the Ed25519 secret seed — no PBKDF2, no passphrase, no extra KDF
entropy||checksum = 264 bits split into 24 eleven-bit English BIP-39 word indexes
Ed25519 public key derived from the seed
libp2p PublicKey protobuf = 0x08 0x01 (KeyType Ed25519) 0x12 len pubkey
PeerId = base58btc(identity-multihash(protobuf)) — the identity hash 0x00 is used because the key is under 42 bytes
algorithm.not_used: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512(mnemonic, "mnemonic"+passphrase, 2048). Feeding these words to a cryptocurrency wallet yields unrelated material and is not a restore path.

$comment: word_indexes are VERIFIED from the entropy; `mnemonic` is documentation carried from the contract, since resolving indexes to words needs the 2048-word English list and vendoring it for one vector would be a poor trade. Verification covers entropy -> indexes -> public key -> PeerId, which is the part an implementation can get wrong.

vectors.name: golden-zero-entropy
vectors.description: The contract's golden. Proves the whole reconstruction path: entropy to word indexes, seed to public key, public key to PeerId. A restore that produces a different PeerId from a checksum-valid phrase is a hard failure, which is why this vector matters more than the checksum does.
